content:
Each square has 4 friends, so the total number of undirected friendship edges is  
\[
\frac{81\cdot 4}{2}=162.
\]

For any friendship edge whose two endpoints have different colors, the two directed contributions sum to \(3\): one direction contributes \(1\), the other \(2\). If endpoints have the same color, the contribution is \(0\). Hence the total sum is at most  
\[
3\cdot 162=486.
\]

This is achievable with a proper 3-coloring, for example color square \((r,c)\) by \(r+c \pmod 3\). Adjacent squares and opposite-end squares differ by \(\pm1 \pmod 3\), so no friendship edge is monochromatic.

Therefore the maximum possible sum is  
\[
\boxed{486}.
\]
